title: Every outward ritual
hook: the Tenth Guru lists outward practices of many kinds and says all miss the secret without love (Savaiye)

segments.voice: Yesterday, bak dhiaan, crane meditation, and your line, not for show. Today the savaiye widen the circle.

Make a list of everything people in one town do to be religious. Some wear something around their neck. Some keep a special object in the house. Some face a certain direction to pray. Some walk to a holy place, some fast, some give to charity, some read the same book every day for years. A poet looks at all of it at once, his own neighbors and his own people too, and asks one quiet question of every practice. Not is it right, or whose is best. Just: is the secret inside it?
screen: `WHAT PEOPLE DO TO BE RELIGIOUS.` → `ALL AT ONCE, NEIGHBORS AND OWN.` → `IS THE SECRET INSIDE IT?`

segments.voice: Two of the savaiye make long lists like this. One, in paraphrase: bathing at pilgrim places, compassion, restraint, charity, vows and disciplines of many kinds; reading the scriptures of many peoples; living on air, keeping celibacy, weighing a thousand opinions. Without the Lord, not one of these counts for anything. The other lists the outward signs of the Guru's world, things people carried, wore, faced and bowed to, the practices of the communities all around him. It ends: the whole world is tangled in false, outward rites, and no one has found the secret of the Lord. The word for secret is bhed, the hidden thing, what's actually going on inside. Hear it fairly. The verse names practices of the Guru's neighbors, but it isn't a list of other people's mistakes. Compassion and charity are on it, things the Sikh Gurus taught constantly, so it can't mean they're bad. It means they're empty when done for their own sake, as a box to tick. Sikh teachers are quick to turn it on Sikh habits too: bowing to the Guru Granth Sahib without listening to it, keeping the outward form while the heart is elsewhere, saying the Nitnem fast to get it done. The secret, the savaiye have been saying all week, is love. A ritual with love in it is alive. The same ritual without it is a costume.
screen: `TWO LISTS OF EVERY PRACTICE.` · `NO ONE FOUND THE SECRET, THE BHED.` · `COMPASSION IS ON THE LIST TOO.` · `TURNED ON SIKH HABITS AS WELL.` · then, large: `THE SECRET IS LOVE.`

segments.voice: Pick one thing you do regularly, religious or not, a prayer, a visit, a call to a parent, a family dinner, and walk through it in your mind. Ask gently: is there love in it right now, or has it become a box I tick? Don't judge the answer, just see it clearly, and if you pray, let Waheguru sit with it.
Bhed, the hidden thing. The savaiye's long lists of practices, and the line that says the whole world is tangled in them and hasn't found the secret.
Your line: the secret is love. The heart, not the count. Day three hundred sixty-seven, done.

screen: `DAY 367 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THOSE WHO LOVED FOUND HIM.`

howItsDone: Many Sikhs recite these verses as part of the Tav Prasad Savaiye each morning, and gurdwara teachers often apply them to Sikh practice itself, warning against rituals done without love.

fork.setup: you've kept a religious habit for years, but lately you rush it to get it done. what would these savaiye ask you?
options: find the heart of it again: is love inside it?
do it twice as many times.
fork.reveal: the savaiye don't say quit, or do more. they say every outward practice misses the secret without love. the fix is the heart, not the count.

original.note: Gurmukhi: bhed, the secret or hidden thing; the verse says the world tangled in rituals hasn't found the Lord's.

trapdoor: what you thought: a verse that criticizes other people's religion.
what it means: a list of every outward practice, compassion and charity included, all empty without love.
what a scholar hears: the two savaiye name pilgrimages, vows and practices of the Guru's Hindu and Muslim neighbors alike, and Sikh exegesis has long applied them to Sikh ritual as well.

chat.says: Do the savaiye say rituals like charity and pilgrimage are wrong?
options: No; even compassion is on the list. Without love inside, any practice misses the secret.
Yes; the savaiye say every outward practice is wrong and should be dropped.
Only other communities' rituals; the savaiye list them as other people's mistakes.
chat.meaning: Compassion and charity are on the list, things the Gurus taught. The verses say a practice done without love misses the bhed, the secret.

bhed.meaning: the secret, the hidden thing inside

notes: Two savaiye paraphrased. The second (usually savaiya 10) names specific practices (carrying a stone/idol, wearing a lingam, facing south or west, worshiping images or graves). The voice deliberately keeps these general ('things people carried, wore, faced and bowed to') to avoid singling out any community. Keeper to decide whether to name them.
The first list savaiya (teerath nhaan ...) includes reading scriptures of many peoples (Vedas, Puranas, Kateb, Qur'an); paraphrased as 'the scriptures of many peoples'. Confirm.
Claim that Sikh teachers apply the verses to Sikh habits (bowing without listening, rushing Nitnem): a common gurdwara reading. Confirm phrasing.
The trapdoor names 'Hindu and Muslim neighbors alike'; confirm this is fair and accurate.
